title: Where You Go, I Will Go

pages.caption: Cover: Ruth and Naomi walk together toward Bethlehem in Where You Go, I Will Go.
Naomi's family moves to Moab when food is hard to find. After the deaths of their husbands, Naomi, Ruth, and Orpah remain.
Naomi sets out for home with Ruth and Orpah, asks them to return to their mothers, and wishes them the Lord's kindness.
Orpah says goodbye. Ruth promises to go where Naomi goes and share her people and her God.
Naomi and Ruth reach Bethlehem as the barley harvest begins.
Ruth asks to gather leftover grain and comes to a field belonging to Boaz, a relative of Naomi's husband.
Boaz greets his workers and learns who Ruth is and how she has worked.
Boaz tells Ruth to stay near his women workers and use their water. Ruth asks why he is kind to someone from another country.
Boaz speaks kindly about Ruth's care for Naomi and her trust in the Lord God of Israel.
Ruth shares a meal with the workers. Boaz gives her roasted grain, and she saves the food left over.
Boaz tells the workers to leave extra stalks for Ruth. She works until evening and gathers a large amount of barley.
Ruth brings grain and saved food home to Naomi and tells her that the man's name is Boaz.
Naomi blesses Boaz and explains that he is a close relative. Ruth stays with his women workers through the barley and wheat harvests and lives with Naomi.
